title: How To Get Control Of Any Classroom
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that when facing a difficult or newly out-of-control class, the counterintuitive but correct response is to slow everything down rather than speeding up and escalating, as many stressed teachers instinctively do. He offers a detailed set of guidelines for what he calls the 'slow down strategy': stopping students at the very start of an interaction until they are quiet and attentive, moving deliberately, speaking softly enough that students must strain to listen, using short direct sentences with gradually increasing complexity, and pausing longer than feels comfortable to draw attention. He warns that the alternative — raising volume, showing frustration, demanding compliance — only produces classroom control through intimidation, requiring a daily battle to maintain. The strategy is framed as a starting point to reestablish order, after which pace and complexity can be gradually increased once the class is calm and responsive.
points: Teachers instinctively speed up and escalate with a difficult class, but slowing down actually restores control more effectively.
Refusing to move on until every student is quiet and attentive, even if it takes many minutes, reestablishes teacher authority.
Speaking softly enough that students must strain to listen and pausing longer than feels natural both draw and hold attention.
Control gained through intimidation requires a daily battle to maintain, unlike control gained through a calm, deliberate approach.
quotes: When confronted with a difficult class—whether a new class in the beginning of a school year, a class you’ve had for a while and lost control of, or one you see once a day in your subject area—the best thing you can do is slow things down to a glacial pace.

When you head down a negative road like this, the only way you can gain control of your class is through intimidation; being mean enough and threatening enough to cause students to cower and relinquish control back to you. If you choose this course, however, every day will be a battle.
Speak softly and slowly. Make your students have to strain slightly in order to hear you. You can even tell them that you’re going to whisper your instructions to see how well they can listen.
Pause often and a beat longer than feels comfortable. This technique has an almost supernatural way of drawing attention to you and what you have to say.
Relax and enjoy your day. If it feels stressful, then you’re doing it wrong. Classroom management doesn’t have to be difficult to be effective.
